source_evidence.observation: For n-by-n square matrices with exact product C = A·B and computed result Ccomp, the paper defines stable matrix multiplication by ||Ccomp - C|| <= mu(n) epsilon ||A|| ||B|| + O(epsilon^2). It identifies epsilon as machine epsilon bounding roundoff and mu(n) as a low-degree polynomial, mu(n) = O(n^c) for some constant c.

The paper does not select a particular norm. It says one may switch between norms using finite-dimensional norm equivalence, at the cost of additional n-dependent factors and a corresponding slight change in the exponent c.

source_evidence.anchor: first paragraph of section 3.1 on error analysis
source_evidence.observation: The surrounding analysis is explicitly a first-order error analysis for absolute error. For a product C = A·B, the operands may carry inherited errors err(A,n) and err(B,n) from prior computations.

The displayed propagation formula is err(C,n) = mu(n) epsilon ||A|| ||B|| + ||A|| err(B,n) + err(A,n) ||B||. The annotations identify the three additive contributions as matrix-multiplication roundoff, amplification of B's inherited error by ||A||, and amplification of A's inherited error by ||B||.

Equation (8) is applied systematically to recursive triangular inversion. The paper chooses to compute T11^(-1)·T12 first and then multiply that result by T22^(-1), applying the inherited-error terms at each product.

ambiguities.impact: A faithful formal statement should not silently interpret equation (8) as an exact identity valid with all higher-order interactions included.

ambiguities.evidence: The paper calls err(T^(-1),n) an absolute error, writes equation (8) as an equality, and then introduces err(n') as a bound for subsequent recurrences. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, paragraph before Eq. (8) and paragraph after Eq. (8)]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization may model err as a nonnegative bound, but should record that this interpretation is supplied by the surrounding recurrence analysis rather than an explicit standalone definition.

contract_plain_english: For stable finite-precision multiplication, the computed product of A and B has fresh normwise error mu(n) epsilon ||A|| ||B|| up to higher-order terms. When A and B already carry errors, the paper's first-order rule adds two propagation terms. In particular, the error inherited from the right operand B contributes ||A|| err(B,n), additively between the fresh multiplication error and err(A,n) ||B||. The norm is deliberately unspecified, and equation (8) is a first-order error-accounting formula rather than a fully specified exact identity. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, Eq. (1) and following norm paragraph; PDF p. 8, printed p. 66, Eq. (8)]
